methods: Prove one missing implication with explicit quantified hypotheses.

original_card.acceptance_gate: Identify the proposition and what would change downstream; do not equate a finite replay with a universal proof.

scope_change_triggers: Replacing a quantified obligation with another finite smoke test.

actual_scope: At each of the 112 pinned ports, owner replica 0, prove exact operator isolation for every finite legal bundle of individually admissible hosted-remainder singleton transfers whose moved axes are pairwise orthogonal; reproduce the all-port singleton census over a receiver domain relaxed to any child with a nonempty full axis list.
scope_change_reason: The catalog card invites an exact hosting implication. This narrows it to the simultaneous-transfer handoff in open PR #3296 and a fixed source-bound schedule. The singleton census deliberately enlarges PR #3190 receiver eligibility; the theorem remains conditional on pairwise orthogonality and owner replica 0, and does not claim a universal all-replica or all-schedule transfer result.
bottleneck_link: A precise isolation lemma extends the finite singleton obstruction to arbitrary finite bundles in a named legal class, while identifying exactly which simultaneous transfers could still affect the construction.
stop_rule: Stop after authenticating the fill, reproducing every scoped singleton and proving the orthogonal-axis isolation implication. Do not infer anything for nonorthogonal bundles, other owner replicas, schedule changes, repairs, or the selected kappa.
evidence: README.md states the quantified lemma and its exclusions; verify.py reconstructs 112 owner-zero port contexts and checks 9,384 candidate transfers, 3,809 admitted singleton replays, exact baseline controls, and a legal orthogonal two-move fixture. RESULT.json records the per-port receipt.
author: Cinna Davis, with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance: source investigation, proof formulation, verifier implementation and local replay.

open_questions.question: Can a legal simultaneous hosted-remainder overlay in the same fixed schedule that contains two nonorthogonal moved axes be excluded by an exact character witness or a written argument?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The isolation proof handles pairwise-orthogonal moved axes. Nonorthogonal bundles are the remaining simultaneous-transfer class that could evade its character selection.
open_questions.first_step: Search the pinned 112-port candidate domain for the smallest jointly legal pair with dot(v,w)=1, then compute its exact eight-stream matrices at the characters v and w before attempting larger bundles.
open_questions.blocked_by: No obstruction for nonorthogonal bundles is proved here; changed schedules, repairs and owner replicas other than zero also remain outside this package.
